questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{″}({x}_{n})},
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ and ${f}^{″}({x}_{n})$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n},$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-4{x}^{2})^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-8x, \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-8x)^{′}=2\operatorname{cos}⁡x-x\operatorname{sin}⁡x-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{n})+{x}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{n})-8{x}_{n}}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{n})-{x}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{n})-8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{0})+{x}_{0}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{0})-8{x}_{0}}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{0})-{x}_{0}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{0})-8} \\  & =2-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2)-8(2)}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2)-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2)-8} \\  & =0.505\,007…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1})+{x}_{1}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1})-8{x}_{1}}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1})-{x}_{1}\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1})-8} \\  & =(0.505\,007…)-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.505\,007…)+(0.505\,007…)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0.505\,007…)-8(0.505\,007…)}{2\operatorname{cos}⁡(0.505\,007…)-(0.505\,007…)\operatorname{sin}⁡(0.505\,007…)-8} \\  & ≈0.025,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{″}({x}_{n})},
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ and ${f}^{″}({x}_{n})$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n},$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-{x}^{2})^{′}=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)-2x, \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)-2x)^{′}=-16\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{n})-2{x}_{n})}{(-16\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{n})-2)}={x}_{n}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{n})+{x}_{n}}{8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{n})+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{0})+{x}_{0}}{8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{0})+1} \\  & =1-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 1)+1}{8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot 1)+1} \\  & =0.878\,555…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4{x}_{1})+{x}_{1}}{8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4{x}_{1})+1} \\  & =(0.878\,555…)-\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4(0.878\,555…))+0.878\,555…}{8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4(0.878\,555…))+1} \\  & =0.901\,873…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}≈0.879$ and ${x}_{2}≈0.902,$ rounded to three decimal places.

questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{″}({x}_{n})},
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ and ${f}^{″}({x}_{n})$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n},$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =({e}^{x}-{x}^{3})^{′}={e}^{x}-3{x}^{2}, \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =({e}^{x}-3{x}^{2})^{′}={e}^{x}-6x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{n}}-3{x}_{n}^{2}}{{e}^{{x}_{n}}-6{x}_{n}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=3.6,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{{e}^{{x}_{0}}-3{x}_{0}^{2}}{{e}^{{x}_{0}}-6{x}_{0}} \\  & =3.6-\frac{{e}^{3.6}-3(3.6)^{2}}{{e}^{3.6}-6(3.6)} \\  & =3.752\,135…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}\frac{{e}^{{x}_{1}}-3{x}_{1}^{2}}{{e}^{{x}_{1}}-6{x}_{1}} \\  & =(3.752\,135…)-\frac{{e}^{3.752\,135…}-3(3.752\,135…)^{2}}{{e}^{3.752\,135…}-6(3.752\,135…)} \\  & =3.733\,407…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}≈3.752$ and ${x}_{2}≈3.733,$ rounded to three decimal places.
